name: Contract Master intake and coordination
precheck: test "$(git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD)" = main && git diff --quiet HEAD && python3 -m contract_master doctor | python3 -c 'import json,sys; sys.exit(1 if json.load(sys.stdin)["result"]["blockers"] else 0)' && /home/d3/.config/orca/cli/bin/orca automations runs --id c0e63d16-c147-40b2-bb1b-5698891f2ff0 --limit 20 --json | python3 -c 'import json,sys; runs=json.load(sys.stdin)["result"]["runs"]; sys.exit(1 if any(r["status"]=="dispatched" for r in runs) else 0)' && python3 -m contract_master turn-check
notes: Moved to ntnsg-rh3 on 2026-11-03 (replaces dc0657b8-923e-4d65-a57f-0a1d8b8ab4a9 on NTNSG-RH1, which is stopped; manager database carried over byte-identical). Created disabled, then enabled on 2026-11-03 after RH1 was confirmed to run no Orca app (dc0657b8 is not stored under user d3 there). Hourly with fresh sessions since 2026-11-03: a reused session made the 10:00 SGT run fail with 'Orca stopped watching this run'. Installed by reusing the former delivery-only automation, so exactly one schedule exists. Orca owns scheduling. Manager commands are one-shot. Run creation is namespacing, not a second scheduler. Reuse and recover a recorded run before creating another. The precheck also skips while another run is still dispatched or any coordinator turn (scheduled or manual) holds the manager's turn lease; Orca does not serialize runs and marks manual runs completed while their session is still working.
